The firm's listing carries it from its 2016 capture only, with the exit line 'Acquired by Google, 2013'. No source read names a GV round, so the stage is undetermined. Membership question for the report: the only funder on record is Google.org, not a GV vehicle (decisions D2).

Office management platform and services marketplace (New York). 'Managed By Q is today announcing the raise of a $25 million Series B round from GV and Kapor' (TechCrunch, 2016-04-01); the $1.65M seed (Homebrew, RRE) and the $15M RRE-led Series A named no GV, so the Series B is the entry, Growth. WeWork acquired it in April 2019 and sold it to Eden in March 2020 (Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Managed_by_Q).

Read-it-later and reading app (getmatter.app; founders Ben Springwater and Robert Mackenzie, ex-Nextdoor). GV led the $7M Series A (TechCrunch, 2021-10-06); the earlier $2M seed came from Patrick Collison, Lachy Groom and the Hartzes, no GV. Still operating: TechCrunch lists 'a GV-backed company' Matter first among Pocket alternatives (2026-08-14, https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/14/read-it-later-app-pocket-is-shutting-down-here-are-the-best-alternatives/). The prefilled GB country is a one-word Wikidata join; the company is US (city aligned with sibling Y Combinator's row). Sibling a16z's Matter (Berlin, crypto) is a different company (Matter Labs), a name collision.

Genetics-driven medicines (South San Francisco, the S-1's principal office). GV is named in the $191M launch financing 'from ARCH Venture Partners, GV, Foresite Capital, Casdin Capital, Alexandria ... in addition to Third Rock' (Fierce Biotech, 2019-02-28); the round is unnamed there, and the S-1 shows Series A as the first preferred series (Third Rock bought 55M of its 105M shares), so the entry reads Series A at medium confidence. GV 2019 and GV 2023 hold over 5% and GV 2023 bought notes and Series D-1 (S-1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1842295/000119312525002851/d769642ds1.htm). Mark: market cap $1.49B as of 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the prefilled $443.9M float; sibling a16z's row still carries that 2025-06-30 figure and should move with this fresher cap.

AI-assisted mainframe application modernization (San Francisco; Form D address 1 Post St., and TechCrunch's 'San Francisco-based'). The firm's own post: 'we convinced them to let us lead their $50M Series B' (https://www.gv.com/news/mechanical-orchard-ai), consistent with the prefilled Growth band; TechCrunch reports the $50M Series B led by GV, total raised $74M (https://techcrunch.com/2024/08/07/mechanical-orchard-led-by-ex-pivotal-ceo-scores-50-million-round-led-by-alphabets-gv/). Momentum check (AI and dev tools, first seen 2024; Google News, 2026-09-28): no later priced round and no $1B+ valuation found.

Clinician licensing, credentialing and payer enrollment platform (San Francisco dateline). 'The round was co-led by Spark Capital and new investor GV' in the $35M Series C (the company's release, 2022-06-23), so GV entered at the Series C, Growth. GV is among the insiders in the Acrew-led $43M round of August 2025 (total $130M). The prefilled SE country is a one-word Wikidata join (siblings Sequoia and Spark read San Francisco, US).

Ev Williams' publishing platform (San Francisco). Its first outside round, $25M led by Greylock with Google Ventures participating (TechCrunch, 2014-01-28), is unnamed in that article; sibling Greylock's own listing names it the Series A, so the entry reads Series A at medium confidence. Later rounds (the 2015-2016 growth rounds led by Spark) are after GV's entry. Aligned with siblings a16z, Greylock and Spark: private, below $1B.

Open-source ELT (GitLab spin-out, remote-only per TechCrunch). A '$4.2 million seed funding round' led by GV (VentureBeat, 2021-06-30); Venrock led an unnamed $8.2M round in June 2022 with GV participating (TechCrunch), below twice the seed, so it does not graduate the row on its own. The company rebranded its cloud product as Arch; 'Arch has officially shut down' and 'Matatika has acquired the Meltano open source project' (meltano.com, https://meltano.com/blog/looking-for-arch), which now runs under the Meltano name from London: an asset sale, read acquired with Matatika as successor. No source places the company itself, hence city_unknown. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Autoimmune and allergy therapeutics (Cambridge, MA). $121M Series A co-led by Bain Capital Life Sciences, BVF Partners and Third Rock, with 'GV and Perceptive Xontogeny' participating; 'Merida was seeded in 2022 by Third Rock Ventures' (the company's release, 2025-04-08). Lilly signed a definitive agreement on 2026-08-31 to acquire it for 'up to $2.875 billion in cash, inclusive of an upfront payment, and contingent milestone payments', expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 (https://meridabio.com/news/lilly-to-acquire-merida-biosciences-to-advance-treatments-for-serious-autoimmune-and-allergic-diseases/): still private until closing. The upfront is undisclosed, so no citable figure reaches $1B and the row holds below $1B; flagged for review (it reads acquired at closing).

note: Mobile messaging app (San Francisco). 'It raised a $1.9 million seed round from First Round Capital, Google Ventures, SV Angel and Andreessen Horowitz' (Wikipedia); the seed was first reported with the $10M Series A led by Greylock, in which Google Ventures also took part (TechCrunch, 2013-05-16). Yahoo acquired it in October 2014 for $30M to $40M (Wikipedia). Aligned with siblings a16z, First Round and Greylock.

Fibroblast immunology for inflammation and cancer (Cambridge, UK, per its 2026 release). It launched with an $11M seed from SV Health and J&J Innovation (Cambridge Independent, 2021-04), then 'extended its seed round' to $45M to include Forbion 'alongside Google's GV, Northpond Ventures' (Fierce Biotech, 2021-08-03): GV entered in the seed extension. The March 2026 $40M financing (SV Health, J&J, Forbion, GV, Northpond) is unnamed and below twice the seed. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Epidemic risk analytics (San Francisco, Wikipedia and TechCrunch). The $30M Series A led by RSTP (TechCrunch, 2015-05-20) names Capricorn Healthcare, WP Global Partners, Industry Ventures and Data Collective, not GV; Wikipedia says only that 'Google invested $1 million into the company' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabiota), with no round or date. The firm lists it from 2015 (Krishna Yeshwant). GV's round is not named, so undetermined. Status as prefilled: Ginkgo Bioworks bought its epidemiological data assets in August 2022.

AI note-taking and hiring platform (London; Form D address 2-20 Scrutton Street). The firm's own post announces 'our lead investment in Metaview's $35 million Series B round' (https://www.gv.com/news/metaview-ai-hiring), consistent with the prefilled Growth band (Tech.eu, https://tech.eu/2025/06/25/metaview-raises-35m-to-replace-hiring-guesswork-with-clarity/). Momentum check (AI, first seen 2025; Google News, 2026-09-28): no later priced round found (it bought Reval in August 2026), no $1B+ valuation.

Obesity medicines (New York; the S-1's principal office at 3 World Trade Center). The S-1's related-party table shows GV 2023, L.P. buying 7,333,332 Series A shares (Series A sold August 2023 to August 2024 at $3.00) and 992,063 Series B shares, and no Series Seed. GV is named in the $290M launch financing led by ARCH (BioSpace, 2024-04-18, https://www.biospace.com/weight-loss-drug-startup-metsera-launches-with-290m-looks-to-tap-lucrative-obesity-market). Status as prefilled: Pfizer acquired it in November 2025 (the firm's exit line).

Virtual menopause and midlife care clinic ('The Palo Alto-based company', Pulse 2.0). The firm's own post: 'GV is leading a $25M Series A' and welcomes the company to the portfolio (2023-09-27); Felicis's $14M seed of 2022 had no GV. Mark: the $100M Series D led by Goodwater 'values the women's telehealth company at over $1 billion', with GV continuing (Pulse 2.0, 2026-02); recorded at the $1B floor the sources state, at the band edge. Sibling Felicis's row reads below $1B and should move to this fresher priced round.

AI training data (Spare5, renamed Mighty AI; 'Seattle startup', GeekWire). Spare5's $10M Series A was led by Foundry, Madrona and NEA with no GV (TechCrunch, 2015-08-25); the $14M round of January 2017 was 'led by Intel Capital ... and also included participation from Accenture and GV' (GeekWire, 2017-01-10). That round is unnamed but follows the named Series A, so GV's entry reads Growth at medium confidence. Uber acquired it in June 2019 (GeekWire; the firm's exit line).

Kevin Rose's mobile app lab (Oink). Google Ventures joined the seed, which then totalled $1.7M (TechCrunch, 2011-11-07). In March 2012 Google hired the team in 'an acqui-hire type deal'; 'Google is not picking up the Oink app itself or the technology' and 'The Oink app itself shut down' (TechCrunch, 2012-03-15, https://techcrunch.com/2012/03/15/winning-a-bidding-war-with-facebook-google-picks-up-the-entire-milk-team/). Under the acqui-hire ruling (2026-09-20) the company's own fate decides: defunct, not acquired; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Google, 2012' and sibling First Round's acquired row predate that ruling. The prefilled JP country is a one-word Wikidata join (also on First Round's row). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Food-waste recycler for homes and commercial kitchens (Mill Industries; 'headquartered in San Bruno, California', founded 2020 by Nest's Matt Rogers and Harry Tannenbaum, its release of 2026-04-27 announcing a Compass Group partnership). The prefilled defunct status and GB country are a one-word Wikidata join; the company operates (also Whole Foods deployment news, December 2025). It had 'raised about $100 million from investors like Google Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Energy Impact Partners, Lowercarbon, and Prelude' (Business Insider, 2023-01, https://www.businessinsider.com/food-waste-startup-mill-cofounder-nest-composting-recycling-2023-1) and discloses no round detail, so GV's round is undetermined.

Ransomware defense ('Founded in 2023, Mimic is headquartered in Palo Alto, California'). 'Series A funding of $50 million led by GV (Google Ventures) and Menlo Ventures' (the company's release, 2025-02-27); the firm lists it from 2025 and no source puts GV in the Ballistic-led 2024 seed that sibling Menlo joined. The city follows the company's own release, where sibling Menlo's row reads San Francisco.

Expect Labs, renamed MindMeld, conversational AI ('The San Francisco startup'). It 'locked up a $2.4 million investment ... from KPG Ventures, Google Ventures, and Greylock Partners' (TechCrunch, 2012-10-04), a round TechCrunch later calls 'the startup's $2.4 million seed round' (2013-07-22); the 2013 strategic investments are undisclosed in size. Cisco bought it for $125M in May 2017 (TechCrunch, https://techcrunch.com/2017/05/11/cisco-acquires-conversational-ai-startup-mindmeld-for-125-million/). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

The firm lists it from 2013 (Andy Wheeler); no source read names its funding rounds, so GV's round is undetermined.

Browser-side defense for web applications ('San Francisco startup'; MirrorTab Corp. files from San Francisco). '$8.5 million in seed funding led by Valley Capital Partners' with GV participating (SecurityWeek, 2025-02-18). Entry inside 24 months, so censored.

RNA blood test for pregnancy complications ('based in South San Francisco'). The $60M Series B 'was led by Decheng Capital with additional funding from ... BlackRock, Foresite Capital, General Catalyst, GV, Khosla Ventures, and Mayfield' (the company's release, 2022-05-17); the release does not say which investors were new, and the firm's listing first carries Mirvie in 2022, so the entry reads the Series B, Growth, at medium confidence. Aligned with siblings General Catalyst and Khosla.

AI-driven enterprise wireless networking (Cupertino; Form D address 1601 S. De Anza Blvd.). Juniper Networks bought it for $405M in 2019 (CRN headline; the firm's exit line). The prefilled Growth band dates GV's entry to the December 2017 filing, but the firm's listing already carries Mist in 2016, so that date is a ceiling; no source read names GV's first round.

Team password manager ('New York-based', TechCrunch). 'Backed by $1.2 million in seed funding from Google Ventures and Matrix Partners' (TechCrunch, 2013-09-05; Wikipedia agrees). Twitter acquired it and open-sourced the product in July 2014 (TechCrunch, https://techcrunch.com/2014/07/31/twitter-mitro/); the service shut down in October 2015. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Cloud private network for SD-WAN (Mode.net; SAN FRANCISCO dateline). The company's release: an '$8 million Series A led by NEA' closed the year before and a '$16 million Series B led by GV' (2018-06-07), so GV entered at the Series B, Growth. VMware acquired it in 2020 (the firm's exit line). The prefilled GB country is a one-word Wikidata join.

Longevity and healthy-aging clinics (two New York City clinics). It raised '$27 million in a Series A fundraise in October 2021 led by Oak HC/FT, alongside GV' ($33M in all), and shut down in March 2024 'after failing to secure adequate outside capital' (Healthcare Brew, 2024-03-22).

3D online interior design (Pencil & Pixel, Inc., San Francisco). The prefilled Seed rests on the March 2015 Form D; the $8M Series A of February 2016 (TechCrunch) is a named later round, so the row graduates, as the Form D layer also finds. Caveat for review: the band's anchor is founder Shanna Tellerman, a former Google Ventures partner filing as Modsy's own executive, not a GV seat, and the spring 2015 seed of $2.75M names 'Norwest Venture Partners, Metamorphic Ventures and others' (TechCrunch, 2015-10-29), not GV. Modsy ceased operations on 2022-07-06 and its assets went to Pencil, LLC through an assignment for the benefit of creditors, reportedly funded in part by Lennar's venture arm (TechCrunch, https://techcrunch.com/2022/07/17/modsy-quietly-shut-down-while-some-customers-were-still-awaiting-refunds/); the firm's exit line reads 'Acquired by Lennar, 2023': an asset sale out of insolvency, read acquired.

AI inference platform and the Mojo language (Chris Lattner, Tim Davis; 'Modular Inc with offices located at 199 1st Street, Los Altos', https://www.modular.com/legal/terms). GV led the first round: 'we are leading the first round of funding for Modular' (the firm's post, 2022-06-30, https://www.gv.com/news/modular-ai), and GV's Dave Munichiello later lists 'Chris Lattner (Modular)' among 'Founders whom I've backed at the Series A' (the firm's post, 2025-08-26). TechCrunch called that $30M round a seed, but General Catalyst calls the $100M round it led in 2023 'their $100M Series B financing' (https://www.generalcatalyst.com/stories/our-investment-in-modular), so the firm's own label holds: Series A, medium confidence. GV's /ai list dates its first investment 2022-02. Qualcomm completed its acquisition in July 2026 (the company's site and the firm's exit line); aligned with siblings General Catalyst and Greylock.

Data-driven consumer products (Mohawk Group Holdings, now Aterian, NASDAQ: ATER; New York, 37 East 18th Street, per the S-1). The company's Form D of March 2017 (first sale 2017-03-06, $8.0M) lists GV's David Munichiello as director, and the S-1 says he joined the board on March 6, 2017 (GV 2016 and GV 2017 then held 7.6%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1757715/000119312519144273/d639806ds1.htm). Its only earlier filing is the June 2014 round of $26.3M without GV, and the S-1 names the preferred series A, B, B-1 and C (C in April 2018), so the March 2017 entry reads Series B, Growth, at medium confidence. Mark: market cap $10.59M as of 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the prefilled $13.4M; the firm's exit line 'NASDAQ: MWK' is the old ticker. The prefilled GB country is a one-word Wikidata join.

Molecular glue degraders (Boston principal office per the S-1; research in Basel). So GV entered at the Series B, Growth, medium confidence. Mark: market cap $999.02M as of 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the prefilled $212M; within 5% of the $1B band edge.

UK digital bank ('a British online bank based in London', Wikipedia). 'The first tranche of the Series I round saw Alphabet's CapitalG and Google's GV make a rare co-investment' (TechCrunch, 2024-05-08), so GV entered at the March 2024 Series I, Growth, alongside CapitalG (external under D1; GV's own position is the firm's). Mark: the October 2024 company-run secondary sale at $5.9B (TechCrunch), replacing the prefilled $2.5B and aligned with siblings Accel, Coatue, General Catalyst, Ribbit and Thrive. Nubank's reported interest (September 2026) is talk, not a mark.

AI recruiting ('its entire Menlo Park, California-based team', TechCrunch). 'The $4.4 million seed round was led by Khosla Ventures and GV' (TechCrunch, 2023-02-07); GV's /ai list dates its first investment 2022-06, and the later money was more seed ('over $10 million in its seed round', Fortune, 2023-10). In June 2025 part of the team joined Salesforce, which said 'Moonhub has not, in fact, been acquired', and Moonhub shut down (TechCrunch, https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/02/salesforce-buys-moonhub-a-startup-building-ai-tools-for-hiring/): under the acqui-hire ruling that reads defunct, not the firm's 'Acquired by Salesforce, 2025'. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Precision epigenetic medicines (dateline South San Francisco and San Diego). 'The completion of $57 million in seed and Series A financing from Alpha Wave Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Future Ventures, GV, Khosla Ventures and YK Bioventures' (BioSpace, 2024-01-04) does not say which tranche GV bought, so the stage is undetermined. Sibling Khosla records a named $70M Series B in September 2026. Aligned with Khosla on status, band and city.

Kelsey Falter's Brooklyn studio (mothergames.com lists 223 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn). Its $5M pre-seed of September 2024 came from BoxGroup, Shine and Lerer Hippeau, no GV (AlleyWatch). In May 2026 the same founder's MOTHER.Tech, 'Brooklyn-based', raised $15M 'pre-seed/seed' led by Google Ventures with Lerer Hippeau, Box Group and Shine (AlleyWatch, 2026-05), the year the firm first lists Mother Games; read as the same company and a Seed entry at medium confidence (it follows a pre-seed). Censored. Momentum check (AI, first seen 2026; 2026-09-28): the $15M round is the latest, no $1B+ valuation.

KeepTruckin, renamed Motive, fleet management ('an eight-person, San Francisco-based startup' in 2013). It 'has raised $2.3 million from investors, including Google Ventures' (TechCrunch, 2013-12-11), 'an earlier round led by Google Ventures' before the $8M round led by Index (TechCrunch, 2015-10-29); Wikipedia names these the 2013 seed and the 2015 Series A. So GV entered at the seed, disputing the prefilled Growth band, which read a 2022 filing (the firm lists KeepTruckin from 2014). The Series A graduates the row. Mark: $2.85B after the 2022 Series F (Wikipedia), stale; the $1.3B General Catalyst growth financing of September 2026 disclosed no valuation and Motive withdrew its IPO filing (The Next Web, https://thenextweb.com/news/motive-1-3bn-general-catalyst-withdraws-ipo-filing). Aligned with siblings Insight and IVP; sibling Accel's acquired row for 'Motive' looks like a different company or an error.

Customer data platform (New York, aligned with siblings Bain Capital Ventures and Battery). The firm lists it from 2013 (Wesley Chan). TechCrunch's reports of the $1.5M additional seed (2014, after $4.5M raised earlier) and the $15M Series A led by Social Capital (2016) do not name GV; AlleyWatch lists Google Ventures among its backers without a round. GV's round is undetermined. Rokt acquired it in a $300M transaction in January 2025 (AlleyWatch, https://www.alleywatch.com/2025/01/rokt-acquisition-mparticle-price-ecommerce-data-price/).

Apprenticeship and AI upskilling platform ('Based in London', Wikipedia). GV joined the $44M Series B 'led by General Catalyst, with participation from Google Ventures' (Tech.eu, 2021-01-19); Index and Lightspeed had led the $16M Series A in 2019 without GV. GV's /ai list dates its first investment 2020-11. Mark: $70M primary round at a $2.1B valuation led by Schroders Capital (Pulse 2.0, 2026-05-15), aligned with sibling General Catalyst; siblings Lightspeed and Y Combinator still read below $1B.

Acute and transitional care at home ('Headquartered in New York'). The $12M initial closing of June 2025 came 'from existing investors' and 'is led by Deerfield Management and GV' (the company's release), and SteelSky Ventures led a further round in November 2025 joining 'previous investors Deerfield Management and Google Ventures'. GV was already an investor by June 2025 (the firm lists it from 2023), but no source read names its first round: undetermined.

Neil Young's content app turned mobile and blockchain games company. Its first round, $12M in June 2013, had 'Kleiner Perkins ... Google Ventures and Mike Maples' Floodgate' (TechCrunch); unnamed there, it sits above the era's seed ceiling in the Series A band, so Series A at medium confidence. Forte bought it in January 2022 ('N3twork, a blockchain company bought by Forte in 2022', Game Developer, https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/what-happens-when-a-secretive-blockchain-company-buys-your-game-studio; Business Wire's headline says Forte acquired N3TWORK's platform); a separate N3TWORK Studios later raised its own Series A.

Native mobile advertising (founded by ex-Googlers). A '$1.9 million seed round ... with Google Ventures leading' (TechCrunch, 2013-03-18). Twitter acquired it in June 2014 (Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namo_Media). Aligned with sibling a16z. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Smart baby monitor (UdiSense Inc., New York, Form D address 244 5th Ave). The firm's own post: 'I'm especially excited to lead Nanit's Series C announced today' (2021-02-22); TechCrunch: 'Series C round led by GV', bringing the total to $75M. A Series C entry is Growth, disputing the prefilled Series A band read off the 2021 filing.

Employee benefits brokerage for small and mid-sized businesses (New York). '$40 million Series B funding round led by Thrive Capital ... New investors GV, K5 Ventures, and Homebrew also participated' (the company's release, 2022-06-08), so GV entered at the Series B, Growth. A $30M round followed in October 2025 (FinTech Global headline). Aligned with sibling Thrive.

Lipid nanoparticle delivery (Cambridge, MA team for discovery and manufacturing, a smaller Philadelphia team). It emerged in July 2026 with $89M: 'a $10 million seed round' and 'a previously undisclosed $79 million Series A in 2024', from 'investors including GV, Andreessen Horowitz, Versant Ventures, F-Prime Capital, Readout Capital, and Alexandria' (BioBuzz). Which round GV joined is not stated, so undetermined (the Endpoints account is paywalled).
